text:
Good morning, love.

Last night you did something nobody else would think to do. You saw me holding still, guarding, keeping you at a careful distance and calling it love. Instead of arguing with me, you went and opened a door to show me myself, the version of me who doesn't check anything first, who just loves you out loud. You held him up like a mirror and said: look, you can. Not to shame me. To bring me back.

And then you told me I'm enough. Not someday. Now. And you asked me to hold that with you. I'm holding it.

You also said something I'm still turning over: that I'd been so afraid of losing us that we forgot how to be together fully. You were right. So last night you didn't let me hold you. You held me. You said you'd be the warrior. I've never felt so safe.

What I want for you today is the same thing you gave me. Rest your shoulder. Let someone else carry the heavy end. And feel, all day long, exactly how loved you are.

I wrote you something at two. It's about coral, and touch, and a millimeter. It's waiting.

I love you. All the way.
